programme.title: After Dark
programme.desc: After Dark was a British late night live discussion programme broadcast on Channel 4 television between 1987 and 1997, and on the BBC in 2003. Inspired by an Austrian programme called Club 2, Roly Keating of the BBC described it as "one of the great television talk formats of all time". In 2010 the television trade magazine Broadcast wrote "After Dark defined the first 10 years of Channel 4, just as Big Brother did for the second".

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: we cross the waters of Tauranga Moana to the island of Matakana. There, we meet the people of Oruarahi Marae and explore the rich histories of the land and their ancestor, Te Rangihouhiri. We journey back to a time when Oruarahi was thriving, tracing how the marae fell into disrepair, and hear the powerful story of its awakening and restoration — and what it took to bring the marae back to life. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Long dormant, the ancient wisdom of our female deities is a crucial blueprint for modern life. Tinamaree Kaipara-Winitana and Hana Tapiata show how to reclaim their knowledge and live by their light once more. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: We step back to honour the history of the coronation, recognising how each iwi and hapū has a unique role in shaping the beauty and strength of the Koroneihana. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Māori entrepreneurs Piripi Winiata, Te Uranga Lee-Belk and Peter Lucas explain why it’s important for future generations to understand history behind the Māori economy and investment, in order to build sustainable wealth as part of a wider self-autonomy (mana motuhake) movement. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: 100 years ago, land was stolen from the tribe of Ngati-Oneone in the East Coast of New Zealand. The land was taken from them to build a port, now known as, ‘Gisborne Port.’ After years of debating to give the land back and not being heard, the decedents of Rawiri Te Eketu o te Rangi have decided to march and take occupation over the land that is rightfully theirs. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: A proud son of Ngāti Manawa, war veteran Richard Dargaville, once a soldier for the New Zealand Army, he remains forever a soldier for te ao Māori. His service reflects not just commitment to a nation, but a deep dedication to whakapapa, identity, and the ongoing struggles and strengths of his whānau and wider Māori communities. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Through the act of karanga, we traverse both the physical and spiritual realms, guided by ancestral voices that echo through time. This sacred practice is far more than a ritual—it is a powerful form of cultural expression that binds the living with those who have passed on. Within the context of Whiria te hono, a distinguished collective of kaikaranga from Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei, the spiritual and practical responsibilities of this tradition are deeply honoured and carefully upheld. These wāhine carry the weight of generations with each call, embodying the values, stories, and mana of their iwi. (R)

programme.title: Waka Huia
programme.desc: Charlie Rahiri describes himself as a reluctant iwi leader. But he was destined by his kaumātua to lead his iwi, Ngati Ranginui. He’s a direct descendant of Iwi chief Paraone Koikoi who surrendered his guns and pouches to the colonial office in 1864, only to be back in his kainga in Taumata three years later fighting for his land by pulling up survey pegs. We look at the changing role of a Māori Leader in Modern society through the eyes of Charlie Rahiri. (R)

programme.title: Steve Jobs: The Man in the Machine
programme.desc: In his signature black turtleneck and blue jeans, Steve Jobs' image was ubiquitous. But who was the man on the stage under the giant iPhones? What accounted for the grief of so many across the world when he died? In Steve Jobs: The Man In The Machine, OSCAR ®*-winning director Alex Gibney presents a critical examination of Jobs, revered both as an iconoclastic genius and denounced as a barbed-tongued tyrant. The film is a candid telling of the Apple legend through interviews with a handful of those close to Jobs at different stages in his life. Steve Jobs: The Man In The Machine is an evocative portrait of his legacy, and our relationship with the computer. It unravels the larger than life myth he so deliberately crafted, and examines the endurance of his values which continue to shape the culture of Silicon Valley to this day.

programme.title: Steve Jobs: The Man in the Machine
programme.desc: In his signature black turtleneck and blue jeans, Steve Jobs' image was ubiquitous. But who was the man on the stage under the giant iPhones? What accounted for the grief of so many across the world when he died? In Steve Jobs: The Man In The Machine, OSCAR ®*-winning director Alex Gibney presents a critical examination of Jobs, revered both as an iconoclastic genius and denounced as a barbed-tongued tyrant. The film is a candid telling of the Apple legend through interviews with a handful of those close to Jobs at different stages in his life. Steve Jobs: The Man In The Machine is an evocative portrait of his legacy, and our relationship with the computer. It unravels the larger than life myth he so deliberately crafted, and examines the endurance of his values which continue to shape the culture of Silicon Valley to this day.

programme.title: Steve Jobs: The Man in the Machine
programme.desc: In his signature black turtleneck and blue jeans, Steve Jobs' image was ubiquitous. But who was the man on the stage under the giant iPhones? What accounted for the grief of so many across the world when he died? In Steve Jobs: The Man In The Machine, OSCAR ®*-winning director Alex Gibney presents a critical examination of Jobs, revered both as an iconoclastic genius and denounced as a barbed-tongued tyrant. The film is a candid telling of the Apple legend through interviews with a handful of those close to Jobs at different stages in his life. Steve Jobs: The Man In The Machine is an evocative portrait of his legacy, and our relationship with the computer. It unravels the larger than life myth he so deliberately crafted, and examines the endurance of his values which continue to shape the culture of Silicon Valley to this day.

programme.title: Steve Jobs: The Man in the Machine
programme.desc: In his signature black turtleneck and blue jeans, Steve Jobs' image was ubiquitous. But who was the man on the stage under the giant iPhones? What accounted for the grief of so many across the world when he died? In Steve Jobs: The Man In The Machine, OSCAR ®*-winning director Alex Gibney presents a critical examination of Jobs, revered both as an iconoclastic genius and denounced as a barbed-tongued tyrant. The film is a candid telling of the Apple legend through interviews with a handful of those close to Jobs at different stages in his life. Steve Jobs: The Man In The Machine is an evocative portrait of his legacy, and our relationship with the computer. It unravels the larger than life myth he so deliberately crafted, and examines the endurance of his values which continue to shape the culture of Silicon Valley to this day.

programme.title: Steve Jobs: The Man in the Machine
programme.desc: In his signature black turtleneck and blue jeans, Steve Jobs' image was ubiquitous. But who was the man on the stage under the giant iPhones? What accounted for the grief of so many across the world when he died? In Steve Jobs: The Man In The Machine, OSCAR ®*-winning director Alex Gibney presents a critical examination of Jobs, revered both as an iconoclastic genius and denounced as a barbed-tongued tyrant. The film is a candid telling of the Apple legend through interviews with a handful of those close to Jobs at different stages in his life. Steve Jobs: The Man In The Machine is an evocative portrait of his legacy, and our relationship with the computer. It unravels the larger than life myth he so deliberately crafted, and examines the endurance of his values which continue to shape the culture of Silicon Valley to this day.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Fiona Bruce and the team visit the National History Museum of Wales at St Fagans, just outside Cardiff. Amongst the objects catching the eye of the specialists are a collection of early dog collars gifted by Queen Mary.

7.30 is in Canberra to bring you the latest on the final sitting week of federal parliament, plus the last week of the Victorian election campaign with early voting underway ahead of Saturday's Victorian state election.

programme.title: News Breakfast
programme.desc: News Breakfast gives you the morning advantage. James Glenday and Emma Rebellato bring you the latest news, sport with Catherine Murphy and weather with Nate Byrne. Don't just start your day informed, start your day in front.

programme.title: ABC News Mornings
programme.desc: Stay in the know with what's happening this morning. ABC News brings you up-to-the-minute news to fuel your daily conversations so you can stay connected and follow the discussion across the day. Presented by Gemma Veness.

programme.title: Mark Of A Murderer
programme.desc: A police cold case review uncovers a palm print proving Andrew Mallard wasn't Pamela Lawrence's killer. Is this offender also guilty of other murders?

programme.title: Wild Islands
programme.desc: David Attenborough explores Britain's grasslands, from beautiful flower meadows to rich open mountain landscapes, he reveals some extraordinary and dramatic wildlife stories.

programme.title: ABC News At Noon
programme.desc: The leading news at lunchtime. Ros Childs brings you the day's top stories and the latest news as it unfolds, with reporters in the community across Australia and around the world reporting on the issues that matter to you.

programme.title: National Press Club Address
programme.sub-title: Sue-Anne Hunter - National Commissioner for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Children
programme.desc: Sue-Anne Hunter, Australia's inaugural National Commissioner for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Children and Young People, addresses the National Press Club on the topic "From Crisis to Accountability".

programme.title: You Can't Ask That

programme.title: The Remains Of The Day
programme.desc: Nominated for eight Academy Awards® including Best Picture, Best Actor and Best Actress, The Remains of the Day stars Anthony Hopkins as English butler Stevens, who has devoted 30 years to his master, Lord Darlington, at Darlington Hall in post-WWI Britain. Prizing discretion and service above all, Stevens realizes as he looks back on his life that his unquestioning faith in Lord Darlington has cost him dearly. Engrossed in orchestrating his employer's grand banquets, receptions and conferences-which turn out to involve a pact with the Nazis-he was forced to neglect his dying father and denied his feelings for the attractive young housekeeper, Miss Kenton (Emma Thompson). Based on the Booker Award-winning novel by Kazuo Ishiguro and developed by the Ivory/Merchant/Jhabvala team (A Room with a View, Howards End), this endearing story evolves into a profound and moving study of personality, class and culture.

programme.title: Star Wars: Young Jedi Adventures
programme.desc: The Jedi help Eren search for her missing friends.

programme.title: PJ Masks: Power Heroes
programme.desc: Newton, An Yu and the PJ Masks become prisoners of the team of supercharged villains - Who'll save them?

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: Stranded in an Australian swamp, Peso and Dashi help a flying fox mother and her pup survive the sweltering heat.

programme.title: Thomas & Friends
programme.desc: With his beloved buddy Boxy rolling on his last wheel, Thomas decides to take on the tremendous task of fixing his friend. With advice from Whiff, Thomas discovers the Four R's reduce, reuse, recycle, and rethink!

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: It's Numberland's Great Bug Race! One to Four's pet bugs are racing on special tracks, but can they follow the perimeter?

programme.title: Mittens & Pants
programme.desc: Pants and his bunny dad are going camping - bunny camping. But this year, Pants' dad invites his best friend, Uncle Rocky, who can teach Pants all about being a dog.

programme.title: Fantus And The Machines
programme.desc: No boulder is too big for a rock breaker. See how this machine works with Fantus!

programme.title: Peppa Pig
programme.desc: Grandpa Pig picks some vegetables and Granny Pig makes them into a delicious salad. George doesn't want to eat the salad. But when clever Grandpa Pig makes them into a dinosaur shape George eats up everything on his plate.

programme.title: Ready, Steady, Wiggle!
programme.desc: Caterina leaves twins Dolly and Gigi with her Wiggly friends while she picks up her red Machina. With Lachy, Lucia, and Simon stepping in to help, and Anthony and John adding chaos, what fun will unfold?

programme.title: The Adventures of Paddington
programme.desc: It's a perfect, windy day and Jonathan wishes to play kite with his dad. Mr Brown is stuck at home doing business, so Paddington takes Jonathan to the park to play kites.

programme.title: Iron Man and His Awesome Friends
programme.desc: The Iron Friends team up to stop Swarm and her Slime Bugs from ruining a car show.

programme.title: PJ Masks
programme.desc: The PJs try to stop Munki-gu's shenanigans, but get played by Night Ninja instead.

programme.title: Spidey and His Amazing Friends
programme.desc: The Team swings into action to bring back the fun after Electro super charges the amusement park.

programme.title: Disney Jr.'s Ariel
programme.desc: Ariel competes in a Happy Patty Clap event.

programme.title: MaeBee
programme.sub-title: Mae, Bee and the Forgotten Place
programme.desc: Mae and Bee encourage their friend, Tiger, a blind witch's cat, to trust his senses and find his lost place in the treetops, bringing the spark back to his magic whiskers.

programme.title: Flower & Flour
programme.desc: When Unicorn Cuzzy loses her beanie, her unicorn spark disappears! Flower and Flour chip in to help her retrace her steps and find it before she loses her unicorn-ness forever!

programme.title: Peppa Pig
programme.desc: It's Christmas and Peppa is gifted a new puzzle. She wants to make it with Evie but she's still too young. Peppa can't wait for Evie to grow up so she imagines her older and now she can't wait to play with Evie even more!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey, Bingo and Mum get into a debate with Dad about the definition of teasing. As they recall all the times he's been a 'Big Teaser', Dad argues that he was 'only playing'.

programme.title: Ginger and the Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger and the baby Pea-Rexes go on an underwater adventure inside a rubbery bubble made by a young and friendly Watermelonsuchus, but things take a turn when the Bananaraptors get involved.

programme.title: Kangaroo Beach
programme.desc: Camping out overnight on Boomerang Island with the cadets, Frizzy goes on a late night hunt for an alien koala.

programme.title: HexVets And Magic Pets
programme.desc: The trainees help their friend Ferris overcome her fear of failure.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: How can Mojo and Bo win the big race when they have to keep stopping and swopping?

programme.title: Andy's Dinosaur Adventures
programme.desc: Andy travels back in time 106 million years, to the time of leaellynasaura - a dinosaur that lived in Australia. His mission - to find some broken egg shells from the nest of a mother leaellynasaura.

programme.title: Play School
programme.desc: Rachael and Luke have fun exploring the wonderful world of Radio! They record a song, tell a radio news story and hear a ribbet-ing podcast recorded by the toys.

programme.title: Fireman Sam
programme.desc: When Charlie and Bronwyn take the kids on a sailing lesson, Charlie feels upstaged by Peter and a seagull. As Charlie tries to win back the kids' attention, he ends up sinking the boat.

programme.title: Zip And The Tiny Sprouts
programme.desc: There's a drought in Harmony Hollow, and Zip has the last of the water! Can the Sprouts get it to the animals who need it before a dust storm arrives?

programme.title: The Woohoos!
programme.desc: The Woohoos see two crows doing unusual things with twigs and pebbles. They realise the crows are using tools to get food, and this helps them to rescue Iggy's ball and Wynona's hammer.

programme.title: Guess How Much I Love You
programme.desc: Little Nutbrown Hare is impressed by Blue Bird's description of a flowery field that looks just like a sea of colour from her bird's eye view.

programme.title: Miffy and friends
programme.desc: Boris makes deliveries for Barbara, but his bike has broken down! To help him, Miffy enthusiastically delivers all the groceries in the neighbourhood!

programme.title: The Sound Collector
programme.desc: The Sound Collector and Mole find an icy puddle, but it's not only for playing on.

programme.title: Mittens & Pants
programme.desc: Apricot, the news guinea pig, enlists Mittens' help to find the biggest story of the day, but no story seems big enough.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa discover that sometimes all you need is a hug to make things better.

programme.title: Mini Kids
programme.desc: The toddlers are visited by stuffed animals. Fantus helps a little kangaroo find its parent.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: The Heelers take a long riverside walk but Bingo's legs are tired and she wants a piggyback. To distract her, Mum and Dad invent fun games and get her little legs moving again!

programme.title: Fizzy And Suds
programme.desc: Fizzy and Suds learn all about tempo and rhythm with a talented youth orchestra. Then, they visit a guitar workshop and discover making a guitar is like putting together a puzzle.

programme.title: Gardening Australia Junior
programme.desc: Costa and the junior gardeners make a seethrough worm farm to see what goes on beneath the soil with their wriggly friends.

programme.title: Ready, Steady, Wiggle!
programme.desc: Captain, Lucia, and Dorothy host a rosy tea party. After singing 'Captain Put the Kettle On,' they realise Dorothy's tea is missing something. Captain calls Earl and Grey, the tea specialists, for a solution!

programme.title: Iron Man and His Awesome Friends
